managers.headline: Glazed and Dazed: Krispy Kremepie’s WR Volcano Erupts, But The Chavenators Out-Bake Them
managers.film_room: Film room smelled like scorched sugar: Krispy Kremepie scored 150.87 and still lost to The Chavenators’ 198.51. Matthew Golden (31.90) and Brock Bowers (22.55) led the counted five while Justin Herbert (19.17) and Daniel Jones (18.80) supplied QB depth that combined for 37.97 — yet RBs managed only 15.55. The three‑week arc (138.25 → 172.84 → 150.87) shows a team living off WR/TED spikes.
managers.bigger_conspiracy: Conspiracy board: top-three share 48.8% and WRs contributed 63.9 points vs RBs’ 15.55 — that positional skew is a bakery that only sells éclairs. Meaningful insight: the roster’s WR-heavy counted output raised ceiling but collapsed floor; because RBs produced almost nothing, auto-lineup correlation suffered when the opponent generated more across positions. Punchline: Krispy Kremepie baked a perfect éclair and lost because the other guy brought a seven-course feast.
managers.next_episode: Next episode: keep glazing the WRs and pray the RB crumbs magically multiply. Savage closer: this loss tastes like burnt sugar on velvet — beautiful, useless, and entirely digestible only by regret.

managers.headline: Wes Mantooth’s Week 9 Gas Leak: QB/TE Tango Implodes into Best-Ball Hiccup
managers.film_room: Film room: Wes Mantooth’s auto-lineup landed 106.54 points and took a 152.09 bath — Bo Nix (20.93) and Josh Allen (16.61) combined for 37.54 QB points while Amon‑Ra St. Brown (14.60) and Pat Bryant (14.6) pushed WRs to 37.85; RBs managed just 26.1 and TE was tiny at 5.05. The three‑week arc (164.18 → 149.89 → 106.54) screams mean reversion: two monster weeks then a cliff.
managers.bigger_conspiracy: In the locker-room mock press, the advanced insight is obvious: counted QB+WR production (QBs 37.54, WRs 37.85) clustered almost entirely in the top-five whose top-three share is 48.9% — that concentration plus paltry TE/RB floor means single-week variance crushes you. Schedule luck 1.22 didn’t help because opponent simply out-correlated Mantooth’s stars.
managers.next_episode: Next episode: Wes will keep auto-feeding QB/WR top-end stars despite volatility; expect more heroic counted sparks but also more spectacular all‑play shutouts. Savage closer: he drafted fireworks and got smoke alarms — someone bring the extinguisher.

managers.headline: docjoff's Best-Ball Blues: Bijan & Mahomes Postage-Stamp Wins on a Soprano With Stage Fright
managers.film_room: Film room: Week 9 autopsy — counted best-ball five delivered 121.45 and still lost 121.45–190.27. Bijan Robinson led with 27.20 and Patrick Mahomes added 22.23, Courtland Sutton chipped 14.25 and Kaleb Johnson supplied 12.80; the counted positional haul read RB 49.4, QB 32.95, WR 32.9, TE 6.2. Three-week trend (112.61 → 176.89 → 121.45) shows volatility: a spike at Week 8 then a fall.
managers.bigger_conspiracy: Bigger_conspiracy: meaningful insight — RBs supplied 49.4 points while TE barely mattered (6.2), so the roster’s counted success relies on running-back premium more than tight-end margin. Schedule luck only 0.78 and a brutal weekly matchup margin of −68.82 explain the scoreboard obliteration: Bijan and Mahomes performed like co-headliners, but the supporting cast didn’t sell tickets.
managers.next_episode: Next_episode: in this Best Ball opera the manager keeps auto-rotating Bijan/Mahomes combos hoping correlation heals the wound; with top-five counted contributors supplying the bulk of scoring and three-week oscillation proving the roster’s boom-bust heart, expect more show-stopping solos and ensemble no-shows.
